Numbers too small for multivariable modelling of prognostic factors

A surgical referral series at a cancer centre: patients who were never operated on do not appear in the denominator, so the 24% 5-year survival is a best case, not a disease-wide figure

Small subgroups, particularly the 15 HCC-CC patients

limitations: Single-centre retrospective series of 32 transplant patients
All diagnoses incidental, so the findings cannot be applied to known cHCC-CC
Resection comparator selected by propensity matching within restrictive criteria

The resection comparator was restricted to single tumours of 1-4 cm with R0 margins and no nodal metastasis — the most favourable resectable patients the centre had — so the finding that transplant and resection are equivalent (p=0.91) is a comparison against a deliberately optimised control, which biases against transplantation and still shows no transplant advantage

Patients with a preoperative diagnosis of cHCC-CC were principally excluded from transplantation at this centre, so the cohort is definitionally incidental and the paper cannot support a decision to transplant a diagnosed cHCC-CCA

Post-recurrence survival was significantly worse after transplantation (9 versus 21 months) and the recurrence pattern shifted from intrahepatic to extrahepatic — immunosuppression appears to change the disease, a finding the favourable survival headline obscures

30 of 32 were living donor recipients with HBV cirrhosis in a Korean centre, so the waiting dynamics, allocation ethics and tumour biology all differ from deceased-donor Western practice
No waitlist denominator and no dropout analysis: these are patients who reached transplant

28027599.bottom_line: The source of the 93.3% 5-year survival figure for 'very early' cHCC-CC after transplantation, derived from 15 explant-defined patients, against a resection comparator restricted to the most favourable tumours and with significantly worse post-recurrence survival after transplant.

limitations: Narrative rather than systematic; no quantitative synthesis of diagnostic accuracy
Imaging literature on this rare entity is small and heterogeneous in classification era

Recommends biopsy for discordant cases without quantifying biopsy sensitivity, which other work in this depot puts at around 50-60% for cHCC-CCA

limitations: Expert consensus rather than evidence-based grading; no systematic review or evidence levels are attached to the recommendations

Recommending abandonment of the stem-cell subtypes rendered a decade of prior outcome data non-comparable without providing any mapping rule, so no series published before 2018 can be reclassified retrospectively
It is a pathology document and offers no guidance on preoperative diagnosis, imaging or transplant eligibility, which is where the clinical problem actually lies
No evidence grading means the recommendations carry the authority of the panel rather than of data, and they have been adopted as definitional without further validation
Calderaro 2023 later showed pathologist agreement on the resulting diagnosis is kappa 0.19-0.37, which means the consensus definition has not in practice delivered reproducible classification

limitations: Single-institution retrospective design
Non-randomised regimen allocation at clinician discretion
Response assessment was retrospective and not by independent review
critique: This is the clearest discordance in the systemic literature: gemcitabine-platinum doubles the disease control rate (78.4% versus 38.5%, p=0.008) yet overall survival is identical to three decimal places of the p value (11.5 versus 11.7 months, p=0.9686). The paper and everyone citing it lead with the disease control rate; the survival result is the primary clinical endpoint and it is flatly null

A 78.4% disease control rate against an 11.5-month median survival means stable disease is being counted as control in a tumour that then progresses and kills on the same timeline as a less active regimen
Regimen choice was clinician-driven, so patients given gemcitabine-5FU were likely less fit, which biases the comparison in favour of gemcitabine-platinum and still yields no survival difference
Sorafenib's 20% disease control rate rests on 7 patients in the later tabulations of this cohort
Of 123 patients only 68 received systemic therapy, and the 55 who did not are never characterised; the cohort's natural history is therefore unavailable as a baseline
30323089.n: 123 patients with cHCC-CCA, of whom 68 received systemic therapy
30323089.bottom_line: The paper that established gemcitabine-platinum as the preferred regimen in cHCC-CCA on a disease control rate of 78.4% versus 38.5%, while its own overall survival comparison was completely null at 11.5 versus 11.7 months (p=0.9686).

limitations: All 42 included studies were level 4 retrospective evidence
Substantial heterogeneity in diagnostic criteria across studies and classification eras
Only 4 studies allowed direct comparison, with small numbers
critique: The paper's recommendation contradicts its own data: pooled survival favours transplantation (41% versus 29%) and recurrence favours transplantation (54% versus 65%), and the comparative studies are null — none of which supports a conclusion that hepatectomy should be preferred

Pooling single-arm survival proportions across 42 studies from different countries, decades and classification eras produces a number with no valid confidence interval; the 29% versus 41% comparison is not a treatment effect but a comparison of two differently selected literatures

Transplant cohorts in the pooled literature are overwhelmingly explant-diagnosed and therefore small, early-stage and cirrhotic, while resection cohorts include large non-cirrhotic tumours; the direction of that bias favours transplantation and is never addressed
Explicitly dismissing Jung's 93% figure is defensible on its own terms, but the paper offers no comparable scrutiny of the resection series it relies on
No waitlist or intention-to-treat consideration anywhere: patients listed for transplant who dropped out are invisible in every contributing study, so the transplant arm is per-protocol throughout
Published in 2018, it predates Dageforde, Kodali, Mi, Kim 2025, Sierra and Kimura, and has been superseded by a meta-analysis using largely different studies that reaches the opposite conclusion
30442549.n: 42 studies comprising 1,691 patients; only 4 comparative studies with 67 transplant and 227 resection patients
30442549.bottom_line: Pools 42 level-4 studies and finds numerically better survival and recurrence after transplantation than hepatectomy with null comparative studies, yet recommends hepatectomy — a conclusion its own pooled estimates do not support.

limitations: Single-centre retrospective design with a small cHCC-CCA group
Readers were aware that the study concerned differentiation of these entities
Case-control design means reported predictive values do not apply at true prevalence
critique: The rule that performs best (three or more LR-M features, 80.8% accuracy) misses nearly half of cHCC-CCA at 54.5% sensitivity, so it cannot be used to exclude a cholangiocytic component before listing

Because HCC controls were deliberately matched 2:1 rather than sampled at true prevalence, the apparent accuracy is an artefact of a 1-in-3 prior; at real-world prevalence of 1-5% the positive predictive value collapses
51.5% of HCC had an LR-M feature, yet the paper frames LR-M as a cHCC-CCA signal; in practice this means applying the criterion would send large numbers of true HCC to biopsy
Pathology was the reference standard only in resected or transplanted patients, so lesions never operated on — the ones hardest to characterise — are absent from the denominator
30552477.bottom_line: Shows that LR-M features are common in cHCC-CCA but also in half of HCC, and that even a three-feature rule misses 45% of cHCC-CCA, so MRI criteria cannot reliably exclude the diagnosis before surgery.

limitations: No limitations section
critique: The paper has no stated limitations section at all, so every caveat below is unacknowledged

Twenty tumours cannot exclude alterations at frequencies below roughly 15%; 'no IDH1/2, FGFR2 or BAP1' is consistent with the 3-8% rates later reported by Gerdes 2026 and Murugesan, and the absolute framing has been over-read as evidence that cHCC-CCA never carries targetable iCCA drivers
The comparator is cirrhosis-associated iCCA only, which is itself the most HCC-like form of iCCA, so the conclusion that cHCC-CCA resembles HCC is partly built into the comparator choice
A capture panel detects point mutations and some copy number change but will miss fusions depending on design, which matters precisely for FGFR2 rearrangements
Cases come from one institution's archive with no statement of how the 20 were selected from the available cHCC-CCA population, and no survival correlation is attempted
30690729.n: 20 combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinomas and 10 cirrhosis-associated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas
30690729.bottom_line: Establishes clonal common origin with TERT promoter mutation as a founding event in both components and shows cHCC-CCA genomics resemble HCC rather than iCCA, but on 20 tumours with no limitations section and insufficient power to exclude targetable iCCA drivers.

limitations: Retrospective single-centre design
Readers were not blinded to the study design
Lesion mix was assembled for diagnostic comparison rather than sampled consecutively
critique: HCC lesions were down-sampled relative to true prevalence, so the reported positive and negative predictive values are uninterpretable for a surveillance population and only sensitivity and specificity transfer

The finding that 63-86% of false-positive LR-5 reads are cHCC-CCA is the single most policy-relevant number in the imaging literature here, yet the paper presents it descriptively without estimating how many patients would be listed for transplant on that error
Readers knowing the design were primed to look for LR-M features, which inflates the measured ability to call cHCC-CCA non-HCC; the 62-71% figure is therefore an optimistic ceiling
All lesions had pathological proof, which requires biopsy or resection — the lesions that go straight to transplant on imaging alone are systematically absent

limitations: Single-centre retrospective design with only 30 cHCC-CCA patients
Imaging interpretation was retrospective and not blinded to outcome
Comparator groups were not matched for tumour burden or liver function

Patients who were judged unresectable, or who had cHCC-CCA diagnosed on biopsy and therefore sent for chemotherapy, are absent from the denominator; the 64.4% 5-year survival describes an operated subgroup only
The 70% atypical-imaging figure is the most transferable finding, yet it is derived post hoc with the pathology known, which inflates how easily atypia is spotted prospectively
Liver transplant recipients are not in the cohort, so this cannot be used to compare resection with transplantation

limitations: SEER lacks tumour size, differentiation, vascular invasion, liver function and recurrence data
Histology coding is not centrally reviewed, so misclassification is possible
Treatment detail is limited to broad receipt categories without regimen or intent

The apparent benefit of radiation and chemotherapy is pure selection: in SEER, patients fit enough to receive any treatment differ systematically from those coded untreated, and no adjustment can recover that

The 8-month median survival is a whole-registry figure dominated by unresected patients and is routinely quoted alongside the 30-60% 5-year figures from surgical series, which describe a completely different denominator
No central pathology review means an unknown share of these 529 would fail the 2019 WHO definition

limitations: A classification document rather than a study; no outcome data or evidence grading accompany the definitional changes
critique: The reclassification is definitional and unaccompanied by any outcome analysis, so it is unknown whether the narrower entity has a different prognosis from the broader one it replaced — yet every post-2019 series is implicitly compared with pre-2019 data

No mapping or transition rule is provided, so the large transplant and resection series that underpin current practice cannot be re-expressed in the new terms; several papers in this depot, including Kim 2025, state outright that their patients were not classified by the 2019 criteria

Moving cholangiolocellular carcinoma out of cHCC-CCA and into small-duct iCCA shifts an entire histological group between two diseases with different treatment pathways, with no clinical validation of that reassignment
The document is an editorial summary of the classification rather than the classification itself, so the operational detail a pathologist needs sits elsewhere
31433515.bottom_line: Records the 2019 WHO changes that narrowed cHCC-CCA by abolishing the stem-cell subtypes and moving cholangiolocellular carcinoma to small-duct iCCA, definitionally and with no outcome data or mapping rule for the prior literature.

limitations: Very small cohort of 21 cases and 21 controls
Retrospective single-centre design
Reference standard available only in operated patients
critique: The headline that combining imaging and biopsy 'improves' diagnosis means 60% sensitivity — four in ten cHCC-CCA are still called something else, which is precisely the error rate that produces the incidental explant diagnoses seen in every transplant series in this depot

The CK19 33% vs 84% gap is the most consequential number in the paper and is a sampling problem that no imaging rule can fix; it undercuts the ILTS recommendation to biopsy atypical nodules as a way of ruling out cHCC-CCA before listing
With 21 cases and 21 controls the confidence intervals around every sensitivity estimate are very wide, though the paper does not present them prominently
Case-control construction at 1:1 again means the reported performance does not translate to a surveillance population where cHCC-CCA is 1-5% of nodules

limitations: Retrospective design
No intention-to-treat analysis was performed
Dropout risk among listed patients is unknown
The authors state plainly that the much longer interval from diagnosis to surgery in the transplant arm inevitably selected patients with better-prognosis tumours
Central slide review incomplete (63 of 75)
critique: The authors' own admission is the critique: a 394-day versus 131-day interval means the transplant arm consists of patients whose tumours did not progress over more than a year of waiting, while the resection arm was operated on within four months. The primary survival endpoint was non-significant (p=0.17) and only the recurrence endpoints reached significance — exactly the pattern expected from waiting-time selection

Because a known cholangiocarcinoma diagnosis was an absolute contraindication, the transplant arm is 100% incidental by construction; the HR of 0.23 favouring transplantation describes what happens to patients nobody intended to transplant for cancer and cannot license deliberate listing
63% of the transplant arm had preoperative TACE versus 15% of the resection arm, so the comparison is also between treated and largely untreated tumours

No intention-to-treat analysis and no dropout denominator means every patient who was listed and progressed off the list is absent from the transplant arm, which is the single largest source of per-protocol inflation available

iCCA and cHCC-CCA are analysed together throughout, and Sapisochin 2014 showed these two behave very differently (51% versus 78% 5-year survival), so the pooled 67% figure is a weighted average of two diseases
The multivariable model in the 2-5 cm subgroup has 45 patients and three covariates, with a differentiation hazard ratio spanning 1.37 to 12.66
32090444.n: 75 cirrhotic patients with iCCA and/or cHCC-CCA 5 cm or smaller: 49 liver transplantation and 26 liver resection
32090444.bottom_line: Finds markedly lower recurrence after transplantation than resection (18% vs 46%) for small cirrhotic iCCA/cHCC-CCA with non-significant overall survival, in a transplant arm that was 100% incidental and had waited 394 versus 131 days — a difference the authors themselves say selected better tumours.

limitations: Narrative review without systematic search or quantitative synthesis
Acknowledges that imaging data generated under the new definition were not yet available at the time of writing
critique: Identifies the comparability problem but does not quantify it: no estimate is given of what fraction of any prior imaging or transplant series would be reclassified, which is exactly what a pathway auditing its own evidence base needs
Because no new imaging data under the 2019 definition existed when written, every imaging recommendation in the review is extrapolated from cohorts defined under the superseded criteria
The argument that cHCC-CCA is now a more homogeneous entity is asserted rather than demonstrated with outcome or imaging data
Does not address how the reclassification interacts with transplant selection, where explant diagnoses made under 2010 criteria underpin current practice
32729276.bottom_line: Explains clearly why the 2019 WHO changes make older cHCC-CCA imaging and outcome series non-comparable, but offers no quantification of the reclassification and no data generated under the new definition.

limitations: Only 19 patients across four centres over 17 years
No multivariable analysis was possible given the numbers
All diagnoses were retrospective explant findings
Wide confidence intervals on all survival estimates
critique: Survival confidence intervals reach 1.0 at both time points, meaning the data are compatible with anything from very poor to perfect survival; the 57.1% and 38.1% point estimates should not be quoted without them

This is the worst-outcome transplant series in the depot (64.7% recurrence at a median of 4 months, 38.1% 3-year survival) and the reason is visible in the baseline data: mean tumour 6.1 cm, 73.7% multinodular, 42.1% vascular invasion, 36.8% beyond Milan. These patients were transplanted for advanced disease believed to be HCC. Comparing this with Jung's 93.3% or Dageforde's 70.1% without noting the tumour burden difference is the central error in this literature

The Goodman type II versus type I finding (61.6 versus 15.5 months) runs in the opposite direction to the handling in Sapisochin 2014, where true mixed tumours were the favourable group only by virtue of being distinguished from pure iCCA; with 8 and 11 patients this is a chance finding as readily as a biological one
Biopsy in 4 of 19, all read as HCC, is a 0% biopsy sensitivity in this series and directly undercuts the recommendation to biopsy atypical nodules as a safeguard before listing
30-day mortality of 10.5% is two deaths and is reported without reference to the centres' overall transplant mortality
No waitlist denominator and no comparator arm of any kind; the internal subgroup contrasts are the only comparisons available
32970878.n: 19 liver transplant recipients with explant cHCC-CCA
32970878.bottom_line: Nineteen patients all misdiagnosed as HCC, including 4 of 4 biopsies read as HCC, transplanted with a mean 6.1 cm tumour burden and 36.8% beyond Milan, recurring in 64.7% at a median of 4 months — the series that shows what happens when tumour burden is not controlled.

limitations: Only 19 cHCC-CCA patients, giving very limited statistical power
Single-centre retrospective design
Comparator groups not matched for tumour burden or liver function
critique: With 19 patients the non-significant overall survival comparison is uninformative rather than reassuring; the study is powered only to detect very large differences and the authors' framing of 'comparable' survival is not supported

The 12.2% 5-year recurrence-free survival against a 44.7% overall survival means most patients recur and are then salvaged or survive with disease, so overall survival here reflects post-recurrence treatment as much as the resection
Liver transplant patients were explicitly excluded, so the paper cannot be used in any comparison of resection with transplantation despite being cited in that context
Biliary invasion at 36.8% versus 5.0% in HCC is a marker that the entity is behaving biliary, yet no analysis links it to the recurrence pattern
Resection series by construction exclude patients found unresectable at exploration or on biopsy
33276780.n: 19 cHCC-CCA resections, compared with the institution's HCC and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma resections
33276780.bottom_line: Finds intermediate and statistically indistinguishable overall survival but a 12.2% 5-year recurrence-free survival after resection of cHCC-CCA in 19 patients, with transplant recipients deliberately excluded.

limitations: Retrospective multicentre design with heterogeneous institutional practice
Authors admit slides were not centrally re-reviewed
Small numbers in the preoperatively diagnosed and beyond-criteria subgroups
critique: This is the most cited source for the claim that transplanting cHCC-CCA within Milan gives HCC-equivalent survival, and the sentence that undoes it is in its own results: only 2 of 99 transplant recipients were knowingly transplanted with a cHCC-CCA diagnosis. The equivalence claim rests on p=0.806 in 67 patients — a non-significant result in a small subgroup, not a demonstration of equivalence; recurrence in the same subgroup was double that of HCC (23.1% versus 11.5%, p<0.001), and that is the significant finding
Within Milan, overall survival for transplant versus resection was not significant (p=0.078) while disease-free survival was (p<0.001); the paper's framing selects the positive endpoint

Tumour burden was classified on initial imaging, not explant, so Milan status here is prospectively knowable — which is a genuine strength — but it also means the 70.1% includes patients whose explant burden exceeded Milan, and the paper does not report how many
No central pathology review across 12 centres over 9 years, in an entity where the Calderaro data show pathologist agreement at kappa 0.19-0.37
No waitlist denominator: patients listed as HCC who dropped out before transplant and were never found to have cHCC-CCA are structurally invisible, so the transplant arm is per-protocol
Two senior authors have industry relationships, and the paper's conclusion expands a transplant indication
33316425.n: 3,206 patients: 208 cHCC-CCA (99 transplant, 109 resection) and 2,998 HCC (2,174 transplant, 824 resection)
33316425.bottom_line: Reports 70.1% versus 73.4% 5-year survival for cHCC-CCA versus HCC transplanted within Milan (p=0.806) with double the recurrence, in a cohort where only 2 of 99 recipients were knowingly transplanted with the diagnosis.

limitations: Retrospective design with pathology available only in operated or biopsied lesions
Operator-dependent modality with single-centre reader experience
Modest numbers in each histological group

All lesions had histology, so the lesions managed on imaging alone — the population the criterion is aimed at — are absent from the denominator

Immunohistochemistry alone without PCR or sequencing confirmation of microsatellite status
Resected cases only, so advanced disease is not represented
critique: 0 of 24 gives an upper 95% confidence bound of roughly 14%, so this cannot establish that dMMR does not occur in cHCC-CCA, only that it is uncommon; the zero is being cited as if it were a definitive negative

limitations: Registry data lack central pathology review, tumour markers and imaging
Treatment sequencing and intent are not captured, so TACE may be adjuvant, bridging or palliative
Grade and other pathological detail are missing in most records
critique: The TACE hazard ratios reverse between strata (0.56 vs 1.64), which is a signature of confounding by indication rather than a treatment effect; neither figure licenses a recommendation about TACE in cHCC-CCA
Grade unknown in 68.7% removes the single variable most consistently associated with outcome in cHCC-CCA, so adjusted models are built on a largely blind dataset
A 55.5% resection rate in a registry means the surgical subgroup is highly selected for preserved liver function and resectable burden; survival within it cannot be read as the effect of surgery
Histology code alone, over a period spanning the classification changes, means the cHCC-CCA label is heterogeneous by construction
34213048.n: 95,149 primary liver cancers, of which the HCC-CC subgroup was analysed separately
34213048.bottom_line: Provides an unselected national 5-year survival of 25.7% for cHCC-CCA, but its treatment comparisons — especially the directionally contradictory TACE estimates — are confounded by indication and cannot guide therapy.

limitations: Narrative review without systematic search, quality appraisal or quantitative synthesis
Acknowledges that the underlying evidence for each modality is retrospective and heterogeneous
critique: Almost all the quantitative material concerns cholangiocarcinoma; cHCC-CCA appears in the title but has essentially no dedicated evidence base in the review, so every recommendation reaching it is extrapolation from a different disease

No distinction is drawn between the hypervascular HCC-dominant cHCC-CCA, which might respond to arterial therapies, and the hypovascular cholangiocarcinoma-dominant form, which the one dedicated TACE study (Kim 2010) shows has median survival of 4 versus 16 months — the single most important selection variable for locoregional therapy here goes unaddressed
No pooled estimates, so a pathway cannot derive an expected response rate or survival for any modality
The review predates the interventional-plus-immunotargeted combinations that now dominate practice in this entity
34283065.bottom_line: A broad survey of locoregional techniques for biliary liver cancer whose cHCC-CCA content is extrapolated from cholangiocarcinoma, with no pooled estimates and no account of how tumour vascularity should drive modality choice.

limitations: SEER lacks differentiation, vascular invasion, nodal status and recurrence
Small numbers after matching limit power, particularly in the beyond-Milan stratum
Reasons for choosing transplantation over resection are not recorded
critique: The entire transplant-versus-resection claim rests on 32 matched pairs, and the within-Milan result on 15 pairs; a single reclassified case would move the p value across 0.05
Matching was done on SEER variables only, so it cannot balance differentiation, vascular invasion or nodal status — the features that actually drive recurrence in cHCC-CCA

Fibrosis stage known in 120 of 736 means the resection arm almost certainly contains better livers and the transplant arm worse ones, which biases survival in opposite directions for reasons unrelated to the tumour

Patients transplanted for cHCC-CCA in SEER were overwhelmingly listed as HCC and diagnosed on the explant; the dataset cannot distinguish knowing from incidental transplantation, so 'transplantation is better' is an explant-defined, not a listable, conclusion
No waitlist denominator: patients listed and never transplanted do not appear, so this is per-protocol by construction
34925507.n: 736 patients with cHCC-CCA in SEER; 32 transplant and 32 hepatectomy patients after propensity matching
34925507.bottom_line: Finds no significant change in US incidence and a transplant survival advantage over resection that rests on 32 matched pairs with no pathological covariates and no waitlist denominator — hypothesis-generating only.

limitations: Retrospective multicentre design with heterogeneous management
Limited sample size for multivariable modelling
Postoperative TACE was not randomised and was given at clinician discretion
critique: An AFP of 200 or more as protective for recurrence-free survival (HR 0.45) is biologically implausible and almost certainly reflects that high-AFP tumours are HCC-dominant and were given HCC-directed adjuvant treatment; the paper reports it without comment

Tumour number carries HR 30.85 for overall survival, an effect size that in a 95-patient Cox model indicates sparse-data bias, and it is listed as an independent predictor despite a non-significant univariate association

The TACE hazard ratio of 0.2 is unadjustable confounding by indication: only patients who recovered well enough were offered adjuvant TACE, so the comparison is partly between survivors and non-survivors
No confidence intervals are reported for the headline hazard ratios in the extracted text, which makes the precision of a 95-patient model impossible to judge

With a median recurrence-free survival of 7.27 months against 26.8 months overall survival, most of the survival signal is generated after recurrence and therefore by post-recurrence therapy that is not described
36405111.n: 95 patients after radical resection for cHCC-CCA
36405111.bottom_line: Reports median overall survival of 26.8 months and 23.6% at 5 years after radical resection with CA19-9, Child-Pugh and tumour number as adverse factors, but its multivariable model contains an implausibly protective AFP coefficient and an uninterpretably large tumour-number effect.

limitations: Retrospective multicentre cohort spanning two decades of changing practice
Small subgroups for every treatment comparison, particularly checkpoint inhibitors
Treatment allocation at clinician discretion
critique: The 15.5-versus-5.3-month chemotherapy contrast is the figure most often lifted from this paper and it did not reach significance (p=0.052) and did not survive multivariable adjustment; quoting it as a chemotherapy benefit misrepresents the result

The comparison is chemotherapy versus no chemotherapy, which in a 2003-2022 European cohort means fit patients versus patients too unwell or too advanced for treatment — the 5.3-month arm is a prognosis, not a control group

The 17.8-month checkpoint inhibitor median rests on 7 patients and is nonetheless now cited as the highest median overall survival achieved in cHCC-CCA; with 7 patients the confidence interval would encompass most of the reported range for every other regimen
Spanning 2003-2022 means the cohort crosses the 2010 and 2019 WHO classifications and the entire arrival of checkpoint inhibition, so the treatment subgroups also differ by era
Only 44 of 101 received systemic therapy and the untreated 57 are the comparator throughout, which makes every treatment contrast in the paper confounded by fitness
36753993.n: 101 patients with cHCC-CCA, of whom 44 received systemic therapy
36753993.bottom_line: The largest European cHCC-CCA cohort: chemotherapy versus no chemotherapy gave 15.5 versus 5.3 months but at p=0.052 and non-significant on multivariable analysis, while a 7-patient checkpoint inhibitor subgroup produced the cohort's best median survival of 17.8 months.

limitations: Narrative review without systematic search or quantitative synthesis
Acknowledges the absence of prospective data specific to cHCC-CCA
critique: The cHCC-CCA recommendations are extrapolated essentially in full from intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and the review does not quantify the uncertainty that extrapolation introduces, nor address the HCC-like genomics reported by Joseph and Murugesan that argue the opposite way
No pooled response or survival estimates are offered for cHCC-CCA, so the review cannot inform an expected benefit or a consent discussion
The extraction of this paper is truncated after the main text into the reference list only, so no limitations paragraph beyond the general acknowledgement of absent prospective data was recoverable
Recommending the biliary paradigm without a mechanism to identify which tumours are cholangiocarcinoma-dominant leaves the practical decision exactly where it started
37174120.bottom_line: A review that defaults cHCC-CCA systemic treatment to the biliary tract cancer paradigm by extrapolation from iCCA, with no entity-specific pooled estimates and no account of the HCC-like genomic data that point the other way.

limitations: Only 16 patients, 9 of them first-line, across seven centres
Retrospective design with investigator-assessed response
No comparator arm
critique: A 33% response rate from 3 responses in 9 patients has a 95% confidence interval of roughly 7-70%; it is being quoted across the 2025-2026 reviews as establishing checkpoint inhibitor activity in this entity, and it does not

Median progression-free survival of 3 months against a median overall survival of 13 months means most of the survival accrued after this treatment failed, i.e. on subsequent lines that are not described

Two severe gastrointestinal bleeds in 16 patients is a 12.5% rate for a bevacizumab-containing regimen in a cirrhotic population, which is a safety signal that the favourable response framing does not foreground

Pooling first-line and later-line patients for the headline and then reporting only the first-line survival means the 16-patient and 9-patient denominators are used interchangeably across the paper's claims
No molecular or histological stratification, so there is no way to know whether the three responders were HCC-dominant tumours that would have been expected to respond to an HCC regimen
38059651.n: 16 patients treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab; 9 in the first line and 7 in later lines
38059651.bottom_line: Nine first-line patients given atezolizumab-bevacizumab achieved 33% response, 3-month progression-free survival and 13-month overall survival, with two severe gastrointestinal bleeds — the most-cited evidence for checkpoint inhibition in cHCC-CCA and far too small to establish it.

limitations: Retrospective multicentre image collection with variable slide preparation and scanning
No prospective validation of the classifier as a clinical decision tool
Survival subgroups, particularly the transplant subset, are small
critique: There is no ground truth: the model is trained on pathologist-assigned HCC and iCCA labels, and the same paper shows pathologists agree on cHCC-CCA at kappa 0.19-0.37, so the classifier is being validated against a reference standard it has just demonstrated to be unreliable

The transplant finding — 45.4% versus 76.4% 5-year survival, HR 2.69 with a lower bound of 1.15 — is the most clinically loaded result and rests on a small explant-defined subgroup with wide confidence limits

Reclassification is performed on resection or explant slides, so it cannot be applied at listing, where only a needle biopsy or imaging is available; the paper is a retrospective explanation of outcomes, not a selection tool

If the entity can be split into two groups with 31 percentage points of 5-year survival between them, then every pooled cHCC-CCA survival figure in this depot is a weighted average of two different diseases in unknown proportions
38092727.bottom_line: Demonstrates that cHCC-CCA splits by deep-learning phenotype into HCC-like and iCCA-like tumours with sharply different post-transplant survival (76.4% vs 45.4% at 5 years), while also showing pathologists agree on the diagnosis at kappa 0.19 — so the entity's pooled survival figures are averages of two diseases.

limitations: Narrative review without systematic search, quality appraisal or quantitative synthesis
Acknowledges that the evidence base is retrospective and that no prospective trial exists in this entity
critique: Table 1 places transplant and resection survival figures side by side without noting that the transplant series are overwhelmingly explant-diagnosed and the resection series contain known, often larger and non-cirrhotic tumours; presented in a single table they invite exactly the cross-modality comparison the data cannot support
No evidence grading, so a reader cannot distinguish a 15-patient subgroup from a national registry within the same table
The recommendation to treat by dominant component offers no method for determining dominance before a specimen is available, which is the practical obstacle
The biopsy recommendation is repeated across the reviews in this depot without any of them citing the 48-60% sensitivity figures that qualify it
Published before Kodali, Sierra, Kimura, Kim 2025 and Hsu, so its transplant and systemic sections are now superseded
38343605.bottom_line: A serviceable practice overview that collates the resection and transplant survival literature in one table and correctly states that transplantation is not an established indication, but without evidence grading or any flag on the selection asymmetry between the modalities it tabulates.

limitations: Single-centre retrospective mapping study with modest numbers
Mixed primary histologies rather than a cHCC-CCA-specific cohort
Radiotherapy-treated patients excluded, so the derived target volume has not been tested
critique: Only 11 of 53 patients had cHCC-CCA, so the target volume being proposed is derived overwhelmingly from other histologies and no histology-specific analysis is presented; applying it to cHCC-CCA is assumption, not evidence

The denominator is patients who recurred in nodes, not patients at risk, so the percentages describe the distribution of recurrences and say nothing about absolute nodal recurrence risk — they cannot be used to decide whether to irradiate

A median of 6 nodes dissected means many patients were understaged at the original operation, so some 'recurrences' are residual disease in never-dissected stations, which systematically shifts the apparent high-risk regions toward the stations surgeons skip
The diaphragmatic finding (58.3% versus 0%, p=0.008) rests on 12 left-upper-liver patients and is the kind of subgroup contrast that will not replicate
Patients who received radiotherapy were excluded, so the proposed clinical target volume has never been evaluated against an outcome
38425471.n: 53 patients with nodal recurrence after resection, of whom only 11 had combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma
38425471.bottom_line: Maps nodal recurrence after liver resection to the hepatic hilum (62.3%) and portal vein-vena cava region (39.6%) to propose a radiotherapy target volume, from 53 recurrence patients of whom only 11 had cHCC-CCA and with no outcome validation.

limitations: Single-centre retrospective cohort of 80 patients
No external validation of the nomogram
Adjuvant treatment was heterogeneous and given at clinician discretion
critique: The 56.4% 5-year survival is roughly double most other resection series in this depot, which points to a highly selected, early-stage, well-compensated surgical cohort rather than better surgery; transplant comparisons that use this as the resection benchmark will understate the transplant advantage
A C-index of 0.809 with no external validation is an apparent, in-sample figure; nomograms built and tested on 80 patients routinely lose 0.05-0.10 of discrimination on validation

The lymphovascular invasion hazard ratio of 11.35 with a confidence interval spanning 3.20 to 40.3 is extremely imprecise, and lymphovascular invasion is only knowable after resection, so the nomogram cannot inform the decision to operate
Transplant recipients were excluded by design, so this cannot be read as evidence that resection suffices
Only 8 of 80 patients received postoperative chemotherapy in the cohort as later cited, so the series says nothing about adjuvant therapy despite being used to argue adjuvant treatment is unnecessary
38965925.bottom_line: Reports an unusually good 56.4% 5-year survival after hepatectomy driven almost entirely by absence of lymphovascular invasion (93.3% vs 35.8%), with a nomogram that is internally derived, externally unvalidated, and built on post-resection variables.

limitations: Single-centre retrospective series with modest numbers
Incomplete nodal assessment in most patients
Biomarker assays performed on archival tissue without external validation
critique: The 30% CCA-component threshold is derived by ROC on the very cohort in which it is then tested, with an AUC of 0.717; it is circular and unvalidated, and it conflicts with the 70% threshold used by Wang 2026 — a pathway cannot adopt either as established

Lymph node status is known in 19 of 72, so the single strongest adverse prognostic factor in cHCC-CCA is missing for three-quarters of the cohort and any survival model is confounded by unmeasured nodal disease

HER2 3+ at 8.3% and FGFR2 alterations at 26.4% rest on 6 and 19 patients respectively; these are the figures now being used to argue for universal genomic profiling, and their confidence intervals are wide
CD3 and CD8 margin densities correlate at rho 0.70 with each other, so they are not independent prognostic inputs, yet are presented as separate findings
All tumours pMMR confirms Yu 2021 but adds no power to exclude a low-frequency dMMR subgroup
39375615.bottom_line: Reports actionable HER2 and FGFR2 frequencies and an immune-infiltrate signal in 72 resected cHCC-CCA, but its 30% CCA-component prognostic threshold is circularly derived, unvalidated and contradicted by other thresholds in the literature.

limitations: Narrative review without systematic search or quantitative synthesis
Authors state that caution is needed in interpreting prior epidemiological studies given the low disease frequency and changing diagnostic criteria
Authors state that difficulty of diagnosis on radiology or needle biopsy is itself the main limitation preventing development of a standard of care
critique: The review's own data undercut the national statistics it reports: only 39 of 263 cases in the Japanese survey were pathologically diagnosed, so the 1.3% incidence, the marker distributions and the treatment distribution are largely derived from imaging-based diagnoses that other papers in this depot show to be unreliable — yet those figures circulate as national epidemiology

The review's most provocative argument — that if treatment is chosen by dominant component then the disease concept 'will become meaningless' — is a conceptual claim with no outcome data behind it, and it sits uneasily beside the Calderaro and Wang findings that component proportion carries large survival differences
Recommends biopsy for atypical imaging or discordant markers without citing the 48-60% biopsy sensitivity figures from Gigante 2019, which are in the same literature
Transplantation is covered in a single sentence citing three references, so a reader would not learn that this is the most contested area in the entity
The corresponding author reports lecture fees from Chugai (which markets atezolizumab) and AstraZeneca (durvalumab), and the review's forward-looking section promotes the two trials of those agents
39936601.bottom_line: A clear review of the 2019 WHO definition and the Japanese national data that also reveals those data rest on only 39 of 263 pathologically confirmed cases, and argues that cHCC-CCA is not yet an independent entity for treatment purposes.
39936601.funding: The authors have no financial support. Conflict of interest: Takeshi Terashima received lecture fees from Chugai Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd and AstraZeneca plc

limitations: Small sample size limits generalisability
Six of 21 patients were diagnosed clinically rather than histologically, though the authors re-ran the analysis in the 15 histologically confirmed cases
Regimen selection was biased toward HCC-directed therapy because of the retrospective design and physician discretion
critique: The authors state that their outcomes were 'superior to those previously reported', but the comparison is against historical cohorts with different and generally more advanced populations; 17 of 21 of their patients were recurrences after prior local therapy and 19 of 21 were ECOG 0, which is the fittest advanced cHCC-CCA cohort in the depot

No patient received a biliary regimen first line, so the paper cannot compare HCC-directed with CCA-directed therapy; the regimen selection bias the authors concede makes the lenvatinib 42.9% response an estimate in tumours pre-selected for HCC-like imaging or markers

The atezolizumab-bevacizumab arm has 7 patients with a 14.3% response rate — one responder — and a median overall survival reported as 'not reached'; this is quoted in the 2026 reviews alongside Gigante's 33% as if the two were comparable estimates
Six of 21 had no histology, in an entity where the same journal issue's reviews state that imaging and markers cannot make the diagnosis; the histology-only re-analysis helps but leaves 15 patients
Median age 74 with 95.2% disease control and only one progressive case suggests indolent, previously treated disease rather than regimen efficacy
Five of the senior authors report lecture fees from Eisai (which markets lenvatinib), Chugai and AstraZeneca, and the paper's conclusion favours lenvatinib
40037890.n: 21 patients receiving systemic therapy: 14 first-line lenvatinib, 7 first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab; 15 diagnosed histologically and 6 clinically
40037890.bottom_line: Twenty-one Japanese patients given HCC-directed first-line therapy achieved 33.3% response and 14.9-month median overall survival, with lenvatinib responding in 42.9% of 14 — but no biliary regimen was used for comparison and the cohort is unusually fit and pre-treated.

limitations: Retrospective design with potential selection bias, acknowledged and partly addressed by multicentre sampling
Suboptimal hepatobiliary phase images in patients with poor liver function may affect results
Transitional phase features were not evaluated
Only cHCC-CCA with rim arterial phase hyperenhancement was studied, so the findings do not apply to the whole entity
Restriction to hepatitis B and/or cirrhosis limits generalisability to other liver diseases
Most included mass-forming iCCAs were fibrous-stroma-rich and therefore targetoid; stroma-poor iCCA may look different
critique: The best model's gain comes from discordance — a high AFP against cholangiocarcinoma-like imaging — which means it only works where AFP is measured and elevated; the 30.8% of cHCC-CCA with AFP under 100 ng/mL remain indistinguishable from iCCA
No HCC comparator group at all: the study separates cHCC-CCA from iCCA but says nothing about the far more consequential error of calling cHCC-CCA an HCC and listing it for transplant

Specificity falls to 64.71% in the best model, so roughly a third of iCCA would be mislabelled cHCC-CCA; the authors note sensitivity rose and specificity fell but do not translate this into how many patients would be mismanaged
Case-control composition of 52 versus 85 with pathological proof in all means the predictive values do not transfer to an undifferentiated LR-M population
Three radiologists read by consensus, so inter-radiologist variability could not be quantified and the reported kappas describe agreement before, not the performance of, the consensus read
40603768.n: 137 patients: 52 cHCC-CCA and 85 mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
40603768.bottom_line: Shows that an AFP above 100 ng/mL discordant with cholangiocarcinoma-like MRI features raises the AUC for cHCC-CCA from 0.687 to 0.807 against mass-forming iCCA, but offers no HCC comparator and so does not address the misclassification that matters for transplant listing.

limitations: Single-arm study with no control group, and 80.4% hepatitis B positive, limiting generalisability
Retrospective and single-centre; findings need prospective randomised confirmation
Prognostic factors require validation given the small sample size
Heterogeneous PD-(L)1 inhibitors and anti-angiogenic drugs reduce treatment homogeneity
Variable intervals for tumour response assessment
Drug toxicity may be underestimated because adverse events were recorded retrospectively outside a trial
critique: The median overall survival of 17.8 months is the best reported in advanced cHCC-CCA and is being cited as such, but 51 of 242 screened patients were analysed — and the excluded 50 who received 'therapies other than interventional plus immunotargeted treatment' are precisely the comparator this single-arm study lacks

Of 51 patients, 11 (21.6%) were downstaged to resection, and those patients' median survival was not reached; removing them would lower the headline figure substantially, yet their contribution is not quantified
The 2-year overall survival of 20.3% against a median of 17.8 months shows the curve falls away sharply after the first year, so the median overstates durable benefit
Seven different checkpoint inhibitors and four targeted agents across three interventional protocols means no single regimen is evaluated; the 'triple combination' is a category, not a treatment

The finding that HCC-dominance made no difference at any threshold from 20% to 80% directly contradicts Wang 2026, which found component proportion independently prognostic after resection — worth noting, though these are different settings and 51 patients cannot exclude an effect
ECOG 0-1 and Child-Pugh A only (all 51 were Child-Pugh A), so this is the fittest possible advanced population and the survival is not transferable to unselected patients

Grade 3 or higher toxicity of 11.8% is far below IMbrave150 (56.5%) and ORIENT-32 (55.0%) for less intensive regimens, which the authors note as favourable but which more likely reflects retrospective under-ascertainment, as their own limitations concede
40666526.n: 51 patients with unresectable cHCC-CCA, from 242 screened
40666526.bottom_line: Reports the best survival yet in advanced cHCC-CCA — median 17.8 months with 41-57% response — from 51 single-arm, Child-Pugh A patients of whom 22% were downstaged to resection, with no control group and heterogeneous regimens.
40666526.funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82072611, 82103220, 82273046); authors declare no commercial or financial conflicts

limitations: Retrospective single-centre study with a relatively small sample, introducing selection bias
The small sample used to define immune microenvironment markers may limit the model's generalisability
External validation in independent multicentre prospective cohorts is needed
critique: The inclusion criteria require no macrovascular invasion at diagnosis, yet macrovascular invasion is the first variable in the final nomogram and is present in 23-26% of the matched cohort; the criterion and the model are mutually inconsistent and the paper does not reconcile them

Propensity matching was performed on variables including the immune markers, but high CD8 occurred in 1 of 19 chemotherapy patients versus 0 of 38 controls and high FOXP3 in 1 versus 1 — the markers that carry the largest hazard ratios in the model are present in almost nobody, so the HR of 0.285 for CD8 rests on a handful of patients

With 19 treated patients and 45 high-risk patients, the 'benefit confined to high-risk' conclusion derives from 13 treated versus 32 untreated high-risk patients; this is a subgroup analysis of a 19-patient exposure

The nomogram's own AUC of 0.689-0.694 is close to the threshold of clinical uselessness, which the authors describe as 'moderate predictive accuracy' and then present as superior to conventional staging on decision-curve analysis
Calibration was assessed by bootstrap on the derivation cohort only, so the reported agreement is apparent, not validated
This directly contradicts Lu 2025's SEER finding of no adjuvant chemotherapy benefit; a pathway cannot cite one without the other, and neither is randomised
40670095.n: 75 patients after R0 resection: 19 (25.3%) received adjuvant chemotherapy, 56 (74.7%) did not; 57 after matching (19 vs 38)
40670095.bottom_line: Reports that adjuvant chemotherapy improved overall survival after R0 resection of cHCC-CCA in 19 treated patients, concentrated in a nomogram-defined high-risk group, but the model has an AUC of 0.69, its immune markers rest on single-digit counts, and the finding contradicts the SEER analysis in the same year.

limitations: Unmeasured confounders including liver function and performance status affect both treatment allocation and outcome
SEER lacks chemotherapy regimen, dose and adherence, so treatment adequacy cannot be assessed
Small sample size, especially in the chemotherapy group, limits power
Residual confounding may persist despite propensity matching
No data on recurrence, progression or subsequent therapies; cause-of-death coding may misclassify cancer-specific survival
Median follow-up of 23 months may be too short given late recurrences
SEER does not distinguish HCC-like from ICC-like histological subtypes, preventing tailored subgroup analysis
Resection margin status is not captured
critique: Eighty-seven transplant recipients were excluded and never mentioned again; this is the largest single exclusion and it means the 32-month median applies only to a resected population explicitly stripped of its transplanted members

The chemotherapy arm had more T3-T4 disease, four times the rate of node positivity and ten times the radiotherapy use, so the numerically worse survival with chemotherapy is confounding by indication; the authors note this but the abstract's 'no significant association' framing still invites the inference that adjuvant chemotherapy is useless
A 59-patient treated arm cannot exclude a clinically meaningful benefit: the matched overall survival confidence interval runs from 0.65 to 1.75, which includes a 35% relative mortality reduction
Because SEER records no recurrence and no second-line therapy, a real effect on progression could be entirely invisible in overall survival

The paper's own discussion notes the chemotherapy group did similarly despite more advanced disease, then correctly refuses to call that a benefit — but the same logic invalidates the headline null result in the opposite direction
40672084.n: 197 resected patients: 138 non-chemotherapy and 59 postoperative chemotherapy; 52 matched pairs (104) after propensity matching
40672084.bottom_line: Finds no survival advantage from postoperative chemotherapy in 197 resected SEER patients, but with only 59 treated patients, a sicker treatment arm and no recurrence data, this is an uninformative null rather than evidence against adjuvant therapy.

limitations: Retrospective single-centre design with limited generalisability
Selection bias central to the analysis cannot be fully controlled in an observational study
A temporal disconnect between intraoperative decisions based on clinical suspicion and an analysis stratified by final pathology creates inherent bias
Median follow-up of 27 months may not capture late recurrence
Including both pure cholangiocarcinoma and combined HCC-CCA introduces heterogeneity that may mask subtype-specific effects
critique: The headline that omitting dissection does not impair outcomes is contradicted within the paper: adjusted progression-free survival is significantly worse in the pNx group (HR 2.12), and the title and conclusion rest on the overall survival endpoint while the progression endpoint points the other way

The pNx group's 59.1-month median survival is an artefact of exactly the selection the paper is examining — 54% of pNx patients were cHCC-CCA versus 19% of the dissected group, their tumours were smaller (3.0 vs 4.0 cm), earlier staged and less often perineurally invaded; the authors acknowledge this but the conclusion does not
Only 26% of dissections met the 6-node adequacy standard, so the pN0 group is heavily contaminated by understaged patients, which biases the pN0-versus-pNx comparison toward no difference
Tumour markers were missing in 56% of patients for CA19-9 and 65% for CEA, concentrated in the undissected group (70% missing), so the two groups were not even worked up comparably
cHCC-CCA is only 77 patients and all subtype-specific analyses were non-significant, so the conclusion about cHCC-CCA specifically is not supported by its own subgroup data
Challenging guidelines that mandate routine lymphadenectomy on the basis of a 30%-compliance single-centre cohort with a 27-month median follow-up overstates what the data can carry
41121221.n: 179 patients: 102 pure cholangiocarcinoma and 77 combined HCC-CCA; 54 (30%) underwent lymph node dissection
41121221.bottom_line: Shows that in a cohort where lymphadenectomy was driven by preoperative cholangiocarcinoma suspicion, undissected patients survived longer because they had more favourable, often cHCC-CCA, tumours — and the adjusted progression-free survival signal (HR 2.12) actually runs against the paper's title.

limitations: KOTRY contains heterogeneous data with the inherent flaws of a multicentre registry, and despite prospective collection this analysis is retrospective with risks of data loss and inter-institutional recording differences
Patients were not classified histologically according to the 2019 WHO classification
A sample of 40 is relatively small to achieve statistical significance
Patients were drawn from Korea, where hepatitis B is endemic
The registry lacks histopathology images, precluding representative photomicrographs
The authors state that most patients had been diagnosed with HCC before transplantation and cHCC-CC was an incidental explant finding
critique: Figure 2A and its accompanying text are internally contradictory: the text states 1-, 2- and 3-year overall survival of 96.4%, 82.5% and 68.6% in patients with MELD 20 or higher versus 71.4%, 47.6% and 23.8% in patients with MELD under 20, while the conclusion, the Cox model (HR 4.27 for MELD 20 or higher) and the figure's risk table (32 patients with MELD under 20 versus 6 with MELD 20 or higher) all indicate the labels are reversed. A pathway should not quote the MELD survival percentages from this paper

A second inconsistency: the text reports 3-year overall and recurrence-free survival of 100% for 'the 18 patients with a single tumour <3 cm', but the figure legend says the analysis covers 9 patients with a single tumour and the risk table shows 5 versus 2 at baseline. The single-tumour subgroup therefore contains about 7 patients, not 18

The portal vein tumour thrombosis hazard ratio of 13.43 rests on 3 patients and spans 2.17 to 83.21; the perineural invasion HR of 5.14 rests on 4 patients and spans 1.07 to 24.69. These are sparse-data estimates, not usable risk weights

All 40 were incidental, which the authors acknowledge last among their limitations; combined with 42.5% beyond Milan preoperatively and 47.5% microvascular invasion, this cohort was listed and treated as HBV-related HCC throughout
Median follow-up of 21.4 months against 3-year survival estimates means the 59.3% and 50.2% figures are extrapolated from few patients at risk (9 and 8 at 36 months)

The conclusion that transplantation is feasible for 'early-stage' cHCC-CC is not supported by the paper's own analysis, in which neither Milan status nor tumour size nor tumour number predicted anything — the significant predictors were all pathological features knowable only after transplant, which the authors correctly concede
41399117.n: 40 liver transplant recipients with cHCC-CC diagnosed on the explanted liver
41399117.bottom_line: Forty entirely incidental Korean transplant recipients with 3-year overall survival of 59.3% and recurrence-free survival of 50.2%, in which every significant prognostic factor was a post-transplant pathological finding and no preoperative criterion predicted outcome — and which contains two unreconciled internal numerical contradictions.

Low numbers in non-European ancestry groups mean ancestry associations must be interpreted cautiously

limitations: All included analyses were retrospective, with heterogeneity in selection criteria and incomplete reporting of pathological subtypes, tumour markers and chemotherapy use

Variability in the definition of survival outcomes, including the time origin of survival measurement, may introduce bias and limit comparability of pooled estimates

critique: The pooled odds ratios compare arms whose tumours differ systematically — mean size 2.19-2.57 cm in the transplant arm versus up to 6.26 cm in the resection arm — and the paper reports this imbalance in its own Table while still pooling. An odds ratio of 0.55 for 5-year death under that imbalance is not a treatment effect

Only one of six studies used propensity matching, so five are unadjusted comparisons of differently selected populations; pooling unadjusted estimates with I2 of 0% produces a precise-looking number that is precisely confounded

The indication for transplantation was specifically reported in only one of six studies, and the authors state most cases were incidental; so a meta-analysis framed as informing the choice between two operations is pooling cohorts in which the operation was not chosen on the basis of the diagnosis

Nearly all patients in both arms were stage I-II (94.8% versus 91.4%), so the analysis speaks only to early disease and cannot address the beyond-criteria patients where Dageforde found 15.8% 5-year survival

The time origin of survival differs across studies (diagnosis in one, surgery in another, unspecified in four), which introduces an unquantified lead-time advantage to whichever arm was measured from the later point
